coverage_requirements.summary: The project status subsystem owns schema validation, exhaustive architecture coverage, and machine-readable progress views.
The stable Gewyvern runtime owns evidence reconstruction and machine-facing validation contracts.
The Linux-first runtime owns eBPF attachment, collection, and physical-host proof.
The GewyLang compiler owns parsing, validation, and lowering into stable runtime IR.
The GewyLang package shelf owns reusable protocol definitions and their validation surface.
The Leserpent 1.x bridge owns compatibility orchestration and persistence while Rust authority is adopted incrementally.
The Leserpent 1.x web console remains a supported compatibility frontend until shared command and query semantics replace browser-owned behavior.
Etragon owns optional advisory learning without replacing Gewyvern diagnosis or Leserpent orchestration authority.
The leselang-syntax crate owns lossless parsing and source diagnostics.
The leselang-hir crate owns validated names, types, effects, and capabilities.
The leselang-vm crate owns deterministic evaluation, continuation, and re-entry.
The leselang-command crate owns lowering into normalized command plans.
The planned leselang-ui crate owns pure lowering into neutral UI IR.
The leselang-observe crate owns validated, sanitized VM/runtime projection composition without becoming an execution authority.
The leserpent-domain crate owns commands, queries, events, identity, revisions, and capabilities.
The leserpent-runtime crate owns transactions, scheduling, replay, policy, and projections.
The leserpent-protocol crate owns wire schemas, compatibility, transports, and shared transport-safety primitives.
The leserpent-adapters crate owns capability-gated external integrations and authenticated Gewyvern transports.
The leserpent-cli crate owns native operator CLI parsing, rendering, and transport-specific error semantics.
The leserpentd crate owns isolated local and remote runtime hosting.
The deployment-bootstrap boundary owns bootstrap-only credentials, daemon and Gewyvern installation state, and explicit authority handoffs before runtime mutation.
Gate 1 requires normalized domain semantics and protocol compatibility.
Gate 2 requires syntax, HIR, VM, and command lowering to suspend and replay deterministically.
Gate 3 requires native CLI parity with Leselang and GUI command semantics.
Gate 4 requires neutral UI IR and a replaceable Avalonia vertical slice.
Gate 5 moves durable authority into the Rust runtime and isolated daemon.
Gate 6 extends the same protocol and UI contracts to authenticated remote and mobile clients.
Gate 7 freezes version-one contracts and requires security, performance, migration, packaging, and rollback evidence.
Every gate maintains fuzz, parity, recovery, accessibility, transport, AOT, and benchmark proof.

cells.next_gate: Keep the 1.x contract stable and preserve loss accounting across future runtime evidence filters.

blockers.summary: The measured matrix still has fewer than two successful physical hosts and two kernel releases; repeated runs on one host do not satisfy breadth.

Preserve the stable owned-text frontend and export contract while extending diagnostics.
Preserve package compatibility and require future catalog filters to retain strict diagnostics and package-root confinement.

Persist the unregistration command ID in each runtime deletion intent and consult receipt lookup before retrying mutation so recovery resolves lost acknowledgements without creating a new operation identity.
Preserve the renderer-only browser boundary and Windows Web compatibility while new commands enter through typed control-plane contracts.
Preserve typed registration and discovery authority while the 1.x Web bridge migrates runtime reads from its managed compatibility projection.
Preserve the stable wire-v1 fail-closed contract; new fields require an explicit schema version while remote-console owns deferred Android client proof.
Preserve the stable lossless syntax and validated span contract while future operations expand through HIR rather than parser shortcuts.
Preserve the stable typed-effect and shared domain-validation boundary as new language operations are introduced.
Preserve the stable deterministic execution and re-entry contract; nested all requires an explicit future protocol version.
Preserve complete current-domain lowering and CLI/Leselang/plan parity as new orchestration operations are added.
Preserve the stable renderer-neutral UI IR and strict patch boundary while mobile or web shells adopt it without frontend-owned command lowering.
Preserve the mature runtime contract and panic-free recovery while daemon, adapter, CLI, renderer, and remote-control cells integrate it.

Preserve the stable daemon authority and isolation contract while adapters and Android/Web clients evolve independently.

WinRM, privileged system-profile activation, and cross-platform product uninstall/retirement proof remain.

Preserve the stable provisioning and retirement identities while future target platforms add independent native transport proofs.
Preserve stable local/remote command parity and zeroized credential handling; platform-native transports remain optional additions behind the authenticated HTTPS contract.
Preserve the stable replaceable renderer contract while release-assurance owns Apple signing/notarization evidence and remote-console owns deferred mobile clients.

blockers.summary: Remote transport, in-app token onboarding, fail-safe switching, immutable private desktop CA migration, stale-fenced endpoint forgetting, private profiles, and real packaged Keychain startup are implemented; formal macOS Apple signing remains, while mobile device proof is parked.

blockers.summary: The candidate schema inventory is now reproducible, but the 2.0 seal cannot complete until frontend parity, remote/mobile conformance, continuous proof, and Apple-backed release evidence are complete.

cells.next_gate: Keep both v1 baselines candidate-only while adding provisioned Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, and Gatekeeper evidence.

blockers.summary: Named deterministic fuzz, parity/recovery, transport, accessibility, NativeAOT, benchmark, app-bundle, private desktop CA, packaged Keychain startup, connection-maintenance, zero-residue, and fail-closed macOS release-pipeline proofs exist. The unified release gate now strictly ingests that machine preflight and distinguishes ready, externally blocked, and malformed evidence. All eight Apple tools are ready; the remaining host blockers are exactly zero Developer ID Application identities and no validated notary Keychain profile. Apple-backed notarization evidence is next while mobile and Windows native evidence remain deferred.

cells.next_gate: Execute and retain Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, and Gatekeeper evidence on a provisioned Apple Developer host; Android/iOS and Windows native evidence remain deferred.

The sidecar remains optional and less mature than Gewyvern's built-in diagnosis.
